concerns.concern: The claim that switching becomes deterministic rests only on rising speckle correlation between On-state frames. No per-cycle electrical data (V(t), On/Off resistance, threshold or delay distributions versus cycle) are shown to demonstrate reduced stochasticity.
concerns.quote: The paper infers it solely from increasing speckle correlation between adjacent On-state frames. No per-cycle electrical data are shown

concerns.concern: With Off periods of only a few seconds, the device may never relax back to its insulating configuration, or may heat progressively. Either effect would raise On-to-On correlation without any 'learning'.
concerns.quote: the device may never return to its insulating configuration. The device may also progressively heat to a higher time-averaged temperature.

concerns.concern: Erasing a trained state with sub-threshold current and thereby recovering stochastic switching is claimed but not shown. The only erasure experiment acts on the pristine configuration and does not test stochasticity afterwards; a train → erase → retrain sequence is needed.
concerns.quote: The only erasure experiment (Fig. 3a,g) acts on the pristine pre-switching configuration, not on a state trained by cycling.

concerns.concern: The fitted relaxation times are one to two orders of magnitude longer than the fitting windows. Only a small part of the decay is observed, so β and τ are almost fully degenerate and the jamming claim based on β is poorly constrained.
concerns.quote: For t ≪ τ the decay is only a small fraction of its total amplitude... In this regime β and τ are almost completely degenerate.

concerns.concern: A single τ is imposed for all aging times while β varies freely. Any real aging of τ is therefore forced into β, so a rising β could simply reflect slowing or speeding of relaxation. Fits with both parameters free, and with β fixed at 1, are requested.
concerns.quote: Any real aging of τ would therefore be forced into β. A rising β could thus simply be a slowing or speeding of the relaxation.

concerns.concern: Bragg peak motion from Joule-heating-induced thermal expansion, or changes in M1/R phase fraction, could cause speckle decorrelation that mimics domain rearrangement. Peak position, width and intensity should be reported versus time.
concerns.quote: Bragg peak motion from thermal expansion. This is expected under Joule heating at 0.26–4 mA and during the 340 K run.

concerns.concern: Sub-micron drift of the beam relative to the sample would decorrelate speckle given the 1.7 µm coherence length. Any drift correction is not described.
concerns.quote: With a 1.7 µm transverse coherence length, drift of the beam relative to the sample at the sub-micron level will decorrelate speckle.

concerns.concern: Hours of focused X-ray exposure may modify VO₂ through persistent metallization or defect creation, producing beam-induced dynamics. A dose-dependence test is needed to rule this out.
concerns.quote: X-ray-induced persistent metallization and defect creation in VO₂ have been reported. Here 2×10¹⁰ ph/s is focused on ~100 µm² for hours.

concerns.concern: The effective sample temperature under current is unknown, with mW-level dissipation, so field effects cannot be separated from Joule heating. The sub-threshold 'erasure' may simply be thermalization; the lattice temperature should be extracted and a heating-only control done.
concerns.quote: The effective sample temperature under current is unknown, so field and Joule-heating effects cannot be separated

concerns.concern: Eq. 1 normalizes by ⟨I²⟩ over the whole acquisition instead of the standard per-frame normalization. Intensity changes could then interact with the normalization and produce artificial decorrelation.
concerns.quote: Eq. 1 normalizes by ⟨I²⟩ over the whole acquisition, rather than by the standard per-frame ⟨I(t₁)⟩⟨I(t₂)⟩ over pixels.

concerns.concern: There is no matched no-current baseline at 313 K over the same duration. Only 298 K and 340 K no-current data are provided.
concerns.quote: a matched no-current baseline at 313 K over the same duration (Fig. 2 provides only 298 and 340 K)

concerns.concern: The β values at 4 mA scatter by ±0.3 and the sigmoid gives a jamming time with very large uncertainty that does not saturate. How the Fig. 4 error bars were obtained is not stated.
concerns.quote: The 4 mA β values scatter by ±0.3. The sigmoid yields t_jam = 4000 ± 3000 s and does not saturate within the window.

concerns.concern: The claim that larger current gives a slower jamming transition, and the shear-thickening analogy, rest on three currents. Two of these are statistically indistinguishable and the third has a 75% error.
concerns.quote: Two of them (1100 ± 600 s and 1200 ± 500 s) are indistinguishable, and the third has a 75% error.

concerns.concern: Fig. 4 includes the 0.26 mA sub-threshold case, where no filament forms. This contradicts the statement that electrical switching induces the jamming transition.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4 includes 0.26 mA, where by the paper's own description no filament forms.

concerns.concern: Reported relaxation times exceed the stated instrumental stability limit, and the text and figure give inconsistent values for that limit. A τ longer than the stability limit cannot be attributed to the sample.
concerns.quote: A τ longer than the instrument stability limit cannot be attributed to the sample.

concerns.concern: The Arrhenius fit uses only a few temperatures and includes the stability-limited 298 K point. It also spans the MIT, including non-stationary 340 K data unsuitable for a single τ.
concerns.quote: It includes the 298 K point, which the authors call the stability limit, and it spans the MIT, where the 340 K data are explicitly non-stationary

concerns.concern: The ~1000 s delay before decorrelation under sub-threshold current could reflect stage or device thermal equilibration after the current or setpoint change, rather than intrinsic dynamics.
concerns.quote: The 1000 s delay could also reflect stage or device thermal equilibration after the current or setpoint change.

concerns.concern: All switching data come from a single irradiated device. The central result should be reproduced on at least two devices and in repeated training runs to test reproducibility and history dependence.
concerns.quote: All electrical-switching data come from a single irradiated device.

concerns.concern: The learning claim relies on a normalized ΔG rising from 0 to 1, but the normalization is never defined. Raw G values with noise floor and error bars are not given, even though absolute correlations are said to be setup-dependent.
concerns.quote: Yet the learning claim relies on a normalized ΔG rising from 0 to 1, and the normalization is not defined.

concerns.concern: Correlation between adjacent cycles alone cannot tell convergence to a fixed configuration apart from slow drift. G(n,n+k) for several k and correlation with a fixed late reference are needed.
concerns.quote: Adjacent-cycle correlation alone cannot distinguish convergence to a fixed configuration from a slowly drifting one.

concerns.concern: Equating β=1 with liquid-like and β=1.5 with jammed is not universal; compressed exponentials usually indicate ballistic, stress-driven relaxation. Strain or thermal drift around the filament could produce this without jamming. The proposed mechanisms should be tested, e.g. via M1/R intensities.
concerns.quote: The assignment "β = 1 liquid-like, β = 1.5 jammed" is not universal and needs a physical model for domains in VO₂.

concerns.concern: The beam is larger than the gap, so the current-carrying Ti/Au electrodes are illuminated and heated. Au(111) scattering, or electrode thermal expansion, may fall within the detector acceptance and contaminate the ROI.
concerns.quote: Confirm that no electrode scattering, or electrode thermal expansion, contributes to the ROI.

concerns.concern: It is unclear which reflection (200_M1 or 011_R) lies in the analyzed ROI at 313 K and under 4 mA, since these separate with phase fraction and strain. Full detector images should be shown.
concerns.quote: Please specify which reflection(s) fall within the analyzed ROI at 313 K and under 4 mA, and show the full detector images.

concerns.concern: The beam covers film beyond the device, while the filament occupies only a small fraction of the illuminated area. The resulting dilution or bias of correlations should be estimated, ideally with a spatially resolved check.
concerns.quote: Estimate what fraction of scattering volume is affected by the filament and its surroundings, and how this dilutes or biases the correlations.

concerns.concern: Novelty relative to known VO₂ memory effects (ramp-reversal memory, phase-boundary scarring, persistent metallic domains) is not clearly stated. It is unclear whether the observed 'learning' differs from these known remnants.
concerns.quote: The paper should state clearly what is new beyond confirming such memory with XPCS.

concerns.concern: The irradiation description is inconsistent: only the central region versus global irradiation. Its role needs clarification, since irradiation is reported to enhance stochasticity.
concerns.quote: The irradiation description is inconsistent: "central 5×5 µm region irradiated" versus "devices were globally irradiated" in Methods.

concerns.concern: Comparing the activation energy to the melting temperature of VO₂ has no physical basis, because a domain-wall or nucleation barrier is not k_B·T_m.
concerns.quote: Comparing E_a/k_B ≈ 2700 K to the melting temperature of VO₂ has no physical basis

concerns.concern: The 1.7 mA data used in Fig. 4 are not shown anywhere: no two-time map, no g₂, no electrical state. Its switching state should be stated, since it is near the threshold current.
concerns.quote: The 1.7 mA data used in Fig. 4 are not shown anywhere: no two-time map, no g₂, no electrical state.

concerns.concern: The 20 nm domain-size estimate ignores broadening from film thickness, instrumental resolution, strain and mosaicity. The direction and measurement conditions of Q_FWHM are not given.
concerns.quote: R_d = 2π/Q_FWHM = 20 nm does not account for broadening from the 45 nm film thickness, instrumental resolution, strain or mosaicity

concerns.concern: The cycling protocol description ('on and off for 3 s') is inconsistent with ~1800 cycles in ~5000 s. On time, Off time, period and exposure timing within the On phase should be stated.
concerns.quote: "turned on and off for 3 s" is inconsistent with the top axis of Fig. 3c (~1800 cycles in ~5000 s).

concerns.concern: Given the low contrast, photon counts per pixel per frame, number of ROI pixels, and the method for g₂ error bars should be reported.
concerns.quote: Report photon counts per pixel per frame, the number of ROI pixels, and how g₂ error bars are computed, given the low contrast.

concerns.concern: The Discussion cites a lack of correlation between positive and negative times in Fig. 3b, but that figure contains almost no pre-switching data. This cross-block correlation should be shown quantitatively.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3b contains almost no pre-switching data. Show this cross-block quantitatively.

concerns.concern: Fig. 5b does not state its temperature. It is unclear whether the thresholds were measured at the 313 K used for XPCS.
concerns.quote: Fig. 5b is not labeled with its temperature.

concerns.concern: The text refers to an 'inset (orange data)' that does not exist in the figure.
concerns.quote: The text refers to an "inset (orange data)" that does not exist.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold current is given as 0.26 mA in Figs. 3–4 but 0.27 mA in the text.
concerns.quote: The current is listed as 0.26 mA in Figs. 3–4 but 0.27 mA in the text.

concerns.concern: The 4 mA On-state relaxation time is quoted inconsistently between the text and Fig. 3h.
concerns.quote: Text quotes τ ≈ 150,000 ± 50,000 s while Fig. 3h gives 160,000 ± 50,000 s.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 2 caption and Methods mis-describe the line perpendicular to the diagonal through t_age. It satisfies t₁ + t₂ = 2t_age, not t_age.
concerns.quote: the line perpendicular to the diagonal through t₁ = t₂ = t_age satisfies t₁ + t₂ = 2t_age, not t_age.

concerns.concern: Eq. 3 is called a 'single exponential' but is actually a stretched/compressed exponential.
concerns.quote: Eq. 3 is called a "single exponential" but is a stretched/compressed exponential.

concerns.concern: The symbol τ is used both as the averaging variable in Eq. 2 and as the relaxation time in Eq. 3; one should be renamed.
concerns.quote: In Eq. 2, τ is used both as the averaging variable and, in Eq. 3, as the relaxation time; rename one.

concerns.concern: Eq. 1 does not state the pixel and ROI averaging explicitly.
concerns.quote: Eq. 1 should state the pixel and ROI averaging explicitly.

concerns.concern: The text describes the Bragg angle as ~50°, while Methods gives 2θ = 50°, an inconsistency.
concerns.quote: Text says "Bragg angle ∼50°" while Methods says 2θ = 50°.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1 caption lumps panels together; panels d and e should be labeled separately, and Fig. 1e should be noted as schematic, not data.
concerns.quote: Label panels d and e separately. Also note that Fig. 1e is schematic, not data.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 2d inset lacks axis labels with units and does not state the number of temperatures.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2d inset: label the axes with units and state the number of temperatures.
